results.title: Belgium Football Team 2026 World Cup Preview: Can Kevin de Bruyne Guide Them To A Magical Finish? | OneFootball
highlights:
The Belgium football team enter the 2026 FIFA World Cup ranked ninth in the world, carrying the weight of a generation that promised so much yet delivered so little on football’s biggest stage. Coach Rudi Garcia leads a side captained by Youri Tielemans, who recently lifted the UEFA Europa League with Aston Villa, and draws on a squad that genuinely balances experience with fresh energy. Their third-place finish at the 2018 World Cup remains Belgium’s finest hour, though the 2022 group-stage exit in Qatar left deep wounds that Garcia has spent over a year trying to heal.
[...]
Kevin De Bruyne, now 34 and operating as a number 10 after his move to Napoli, arrives fit and is expected to start every match, bringing a passing range and match intelligence that very few players on the planet can replicate. Jeremy Doku produced 21 goal contributions in 50 games across all competitions this season and possesses a burst of acceleration that can strand any full-back in the world, while Amadou Onana and Youri Tielemans replicate their Aston Villa midfield partnership at the international level, giving Garcia a physically dominant yet technically gifted engine room.
[...]
However, the concerns are genuinely serious in certain areas. Romelu Lukaku played only around an hour of competitive football this season due to recurring muscle injuries and scored just once for Napoli, meaning Garcia effectively selected a striker on reputation rather than form. Defensively, Belgium look considerably less solid beyond the imposing presence of Thibaut Courtois in goal, with questions hanging over whether the young centre-back partnership can hold firm against elite attacking opponents in the knockout stages.
[...]
The most widely predicted starting XI in a 4-3-3 formation reads: Courtois; Meunier, Mechele, Theate, Castagne; Tielemans, De Bruyne, Witsel; Trossard, Lukaku, Doku, though Garcia may shift toward a 4-2-3-1 depending on the opposition. Group G pairs Belgium against Egypt, Iran, and New Zealand, a draw that most analysts regard as thoroughly winnable.
[...]
### Tournament Prediction:
[...]
Realistically, Belgium should reach the quarter-finals with reasonable comfort, topping Group G before going through the round of 32. A semi-final run looks possible if the draw opens favourably and Lukaku rediscovers even a fraction of his best form, but the fragile defence and ageing spine of the side suggest that a repeat of 2018’s third-place heroics represents the most likely ceiling.
[...]
The Belgium football team possess the individual quality like England to surprise anyone on a good day, yet tournament football punishes inconsistency, and this squad carries too many fitness question marks to inspire full confidence.

# Belgium FIFA World Cup 2026 preview — Red Devils look for success in last dance of De Bruyne
[...]
## Belgium will hope some of its ageing icons of European football — like Kevin de Bruyne, Romelu Lukaku and Thibaut Courtois — can have a potential final World Cup to remember.
[...]
Belgium is still the favourite to top Group G, but it no longer enters tournaments with the same certainty that surrounded its golden generation.
[...]
The squad still has star power. De Bruyne can control a match, Courtois remains elite when fit, Lukaku is the country’s record scorer, and Doku gives the attack the kind of pace that can break a tight game open.
[...]
But this Belgium is also balancing age, injury history and transition. Lukaku’s fitness has been a major talking point, while De Bruyne, Courtois and Witsel are no longer carrying the team into a new cycle. Garcia has younger options in Onana, De Cuyper, Debast, De Ketelaere and Fernandez-Pardo, but the question is whether the blend can function quickly in tournament football.
[...]
The opener against Egypt is the group’s most important match for Belgium. Win it, and it can control the section before facing Iran and New Zealand. Failing to win, and the pressure shifts quickly, especially with Iran likely to make the second game awkward.
[...]
Belgium should qualify, and first place remains the realistic target. The deeper question is whether it can still look like a team capable of causing trouble beyond the group stage.
[...]
Kevin De Bruyne still changes Belgium’s ceiling. His passing range, set-piece delivery and ability to control tempo remain central to its attacking structure. If Belgium is to manage matches and avoid chaos, he will be the player expected to set the rhythm.
[...]
Garcia has inherited a side between eras. His task is not only to get Belgium through the group, but also to make the older core and younger players fit into one structure. Managing Lukaku’s fitness and protecting an ageing spine will be central to Belgium’s tournament.
[...]
